samples.summary: `normalizeSingleCellGrid` re-keys ANY one-cell grid onto the active cell's anchor, even when that cell is not covered by a merge — an HTML paste whose only non-empty cell is not the top-left lands in the wrong cell
samples.evidence: `normalizeSingleCellGrid(grid, anchor)` (sheet.ts:2490-2498) only checks `grid.size !== 1` and `sref === anchorSref`; it never checks that the grid's single cell is *covered by the merged block anchored at* `anchorStart`. On the HTML path (sheet.ts:2385) `html2grid` skips cells with no text and no inline style (`grids.ts:179: if (!text && !el.style.cssText) continue;`), so copying e.g. A1:C1 where only C1 has content produces a grid `{C1: 'x'}` while `this.activeCell`/`anchorStart` is A1. `anchorStart` !== 'C1', so the value is silently rewritten into A1 instead of C1 — a wrong-position write on a plain, unmerged sheet. Even with merges present, the function relocates a cell that may belong to no block at all. The guard should be `this.normalizeRefToAnchor(parseRef(sref))` on the grid's own cell, not a blanket move to the active cell's anchor.

samples.summary: `undo`/`redo` renumber cells (structural undo) but do not clear the copy buffer, bypassing the new `shiftCells`/`moveCells` invalidation invariant
samples.evidence: The new doc on `clearCopyBuffer` (sheet.ts:2217-2222) states "every edit that renumbers the cells it snapshotted (`shiftCells`, `moveCells`) must call this", and the diff adds the call in both. But `undo()` (sheet.ts:5306) and `redo()` (sheet.ts:5338) re-load merges/dimensions/freeze from the store and can undo an insert/delete of rows or a row reorder — which renumbers exactly those cells — without calling `clearCopyBuffer()`. Sequence: insert rows → copy A1:B1 (merged) → Ctrl+Z (row insert undone, everything shifts) → Ctrl+V: `paste` still matches the clipboard text, relocates the grid from the stale `sourceRange`, and now also re-creates merged blocks at stale coordinates (`planPasteMerges`/`applyPasteMerges`). Before this change the view cleared the buffer after every paste, so the window in which a stale buffer could be used was much smaller. The same gap exists for remote collaborators' structural edits, which never go through this Sheet's `shiftCells`.
searchedFor: grep clearCopyBuffer across repo (only sheet.ts:1345, 1562, view/worksheet.ts:5118)

samples.summary: External (TSV/HTML) multi-cell pastes have no merge guard: values are written into cells a merged block covers and become invisible until an unmerge
samples.evidence: The internal path now refuses a paste that clips a merged block (`merge-paste-partial`) and `clearCellsUnderMerge` exists precisely so no content hides under a block. The external paths (sheet.ts:2385 and 2392) run `html2grid`/`string2grid` straight into `setGrid` with no merge check at all: pasting `x\ty` while the active cell A3 is covered by block A2:A4 writes 'x' into A3, where it is invisible and resurfaces on unmerge. The change's own new test ('should not shift a multi-cell external paste off the selected row') asserts B3='y' and says nothing about the hidden A3. Pre-existing behaviour, but the change hard-codes it while fixing the identical hazard on the internal path.
searchedFor: grep getMergesIntersecting call sites in sheet.ts

samples.summary: `shiftCells` now persists the freeze pane only when the final value differs from the pre-shift value, but the store-level shift has already written an unsnapped value — they can diverge
samples.evidence: The old code called `store.setFreezePane` unconditionally inside each adjustment branch; the new code writes only `if (frozenBefore.rows !== this.frozenRows || frozenBefore.cols !== this.frozenCols)` (sheet.ts:1428-1433). `YorkieStore.shiftCells` runs `applyWorksheetShift` → `shiftWorksheetViewState` (worksheet-structure.ts:249-265), which has already written the *unsnapped* shifted value into the document; the comment there (lines 178-182) explicitly relies on `Sheet` re-writing the absolute value afterwards. When the snap restores exactly the pre-shift number (e.g. frozenRows=5 with a block A4:A6 loaded from a straddling document, delete row 1 → 4 → snap back to 5), `frozenBefore === final` and no write happens, leaving the persisted/collaborator value at 4 while this client holds 5. MemStore does not shift the freeze pane, so the sheets suite cannot catch this.

samples.summary: `loadFreezePane` does not apply `snapFreezePastMerges`, so the new no-straddling invariant is not enforced for documents loaded from the store, undo/redo, or remote freeze changes
samples.evidence: `setFreezePane` (sheet.ts:523) now snaps the boundary past any merged block it would cut, and `planPasteMerges`/`moveRangeTo`/`moveCells` refuse operations that would create that state. `loadFreezePane` (sheet.ts:565-569) assigns `frozenRows`/`frozenCols` straight from `store.getFreezePane()` with no snapping, and it is the path used on open (view/worksheet.ts:433) and after every undo/redo (sheet.ts:5313, 5345). A document written by an older client, by the REST API (`applyWorksheetShift`, which is merge-unaware), or by a collaborator can therefore hold a straddling boundary; the renderer then paints a block across the freeze seam and legitimate drag-moves/pastes get refused with no way for the user to fix the boundary except re-freezing.
searchedFor: grep frozenRows|setFreezePane|loadFreezePane across packages/sheets and packages/frontend src

samples.summary: `selectPastedRange` now stores the same `Ref` object in both `activeCell` and `ranges[0][0]` (previously two distinct literals)
samples.evidence: `const [from, to] = pastedRange ?? rangeOf(grid); ... this.activeCell = from; this.ranges = [[from, to]];` (sheet.ts:2736-2744). The old code built separate object literals for the active cell and each range corner. Any in-place mutation of a Ref (the codebase does mutate range corners, e.g. `resizeRange` at sheet.ts:4246/4252, which only avoids damage because it clones first) would now silently move the active cell and the selection together. Latent aliasing hazard rather than an observed failure.

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as described. `normalizeSingleCellGrid` (sheet.ts:2490-2498) re-keys any single-entry grid onto `anchor` after checking only `grid.size !== 1` and `sref === anchorSref`; it never verifies the grid's cell is covered by the merged block anchored at `anchor`. `anchorStart` (sheet.ts:2329) equals `activeCell` when no merge covers it (getAnchorSrefForRef, sheet.ts:877-881 returns `sref` itself). On the spreadsheet-HTML paste path (sheet.ts:2385-2388) `html2grid` skips empty, unstyled cells (grids.ts:179) while the column index still advances (grids.ts:229), so copying e.g. A1:C1 where only C1 has content yields a one-cell grid keyed at C1 with destRef A1; the value is then silently rewritten into A1 and written via setGrid (sheet.ts:2407) — a wrong-position write, potentially overwriting an unrelated cell, on a plain unmerged sheet. No guard exists at either call site (sheet.ts:2385, sheet.ts:2392) nor between normalization and setGrid. The TSV path is incidentally protected because string2grid emits empty strings for blank columns (grids.ts:113-126), but the HTML path is not. This is a logic/correctness defect (wrong condition leading to data landing in the wrong cell), squarely in the correctness lane.

The external paths (sheet.ts:2385 and 2392) run `html2grid`/`string2grid` straight into `setGrid` with no merge check at all: pasting `x\ty` while the active cell A3 is covered by block A2:A4 writes 'x' into A3, where it is invisible and resurfaces on unmerge. verdict.reason: The external (TSV/HTML) paste branches build the grid from `this.activeCell` and pass it only through `normalizeSingleCellGrid`, which is a no-op for grids larger than one cell (sheet.ts:2383-2399, 2490-2498). Nothing downstream re-adds merge awareness: `applyInputInferenceToGrid` only infers values (sheet.ts:1122-1133); `Worksheet.setGrid` forwards raw srefs to the store (sheet.ts:1034-1036) and `MemStore.setGrid` writes them verbatim with no anchor normalization (store/memory.ts:260-266), unlike `set`/`get` which do normalize (sheet.ts:1021,1028); and `applyPasteMerges` early-returns when both merge lists are empty, which is exactly the external case (sheet.ts:2311-2316, 2644), so `clearCellsUnderMerge` never runs. No caller pre-checks either (view/worksheet.ts:4914-4952, view/spreadsheet.ts:698-728, frontend sheet-view.tsx:776). The new test itself exercises the scenario — `selectRow(3)` under merge A2:A4 then `paste({text:'x\ty'})` — producing a 2-cell grid keyed A3/B3, so 'x' lands in covered cell A3 and is asserted nowhere (merge.test.ts:994-1009). `unmergeSelection` deletes the block without clearing covered cells (sheet.ts:4868-4902), so the hidden value resurfaces as stale data, breaking the invariant that `clearCellsUnderMerge` exists to maintain (sheet.ts:2676-2681) and that the internal path enforces via `merge-paste-partial` (sheet.ts:2581-2583). Real, reachable in normal use, and a data-integrity/broken-invariant defect in the correctness lane.

mergedFrom.summary: `selectPastedRange` still uses the pasted grid's bounding box, so a paste that re-creates merged blocks selects a region smaller than what was pasted (a single merged block collapses to a one-cell selection)

finding.summary: `paste` normalizes the *origin of the whole pasted grid* to a merge anchor, so a multi-cell paste onto a row/column selection whose head cell is merge-covered lands one or more rows/columns off and overwrites unrelated cells
finding.evidence: `const destStart = this.normalizeRefToAnchor(this.activeCell);` (sheet.ts:2241) feeds `string2grid(destStart, text)` (2294), `html2grid(destStart, ...)` (2290) and `relocateGrid(..., destStart)` (2248). `selectRow(row)` sets `activeCell = { r: row, c: 1 }` (sheet.ts:3443) without normalizing. With a vertical merge A2:A4 and `selectRow(3)`, destStart becomes A2, so pasting a full row `x\ty\tz` writes A2/B2/C2 instead of A3/B3/C3 — it silently overwrites row 2's B and C (which are not merged at all) and leaves row 3 untouched. Same for `selectColumn(col)` (sheet.ts:3456) with a horizontal merge in row 1: the whole paste shifts a column left. The new behaviour is only needed for the single-cell/anchor case the diff's own comment describes; shifting the grid origin for a multi-cell paste is a destination error, not an anchor normalization. The added tests only cover single-column/single-value cases (merge.test.ts `should paste an external grid from the anchor too`), so the wrong-row multi-column case is untested.

verdict.reason: The quoted code does not exist. In `paste`, the normalized anchor (`anchorStart`, sheet.ts:2329) is never used as the origin of a multi-cell grid. For internal pastes, sheet.ts:2333-2335 selects `destStart = isCollapsedRange(sourceRange) ? anchorStart : this.activeCell`, so a multi-cell copy relocates from the raw, un-normalized `activeCell` (2338). For external pastes, the grid is built from the raw active cell — `html2grid(html, this.activeCell)` (2386) and `string2grid(this.activeCell, text)` (2393) — and only then passed to `normalizeSingleCellGrid`, which returns the grid untouched unless it holds exactly one cell (`if (grid.size !== 1) return grid;`, 2491). The comment at 2322-2328 names this exact `selectRow`/`selectColumn`/`selectAllCells` hazard as the reason the origin is not normalized for multi-cell pastes. Replaying the finding's scenario: `selectRow(3)` sets `activeCell = {r:3,c:1}` (3564); `string2grid({r:3,c:1}, 'x\ty\tz')` yields a 3-entry grid, so `normalizeSingleCellGrid` is a no-op and the paste lands on A3/B3/C3, not A2/B2/C2. `string2grid`/`html2grid` have no other src call sites, so there is no alternate paste path with the described shape.
